objective: Run one arm of the ONERA M6 vcoarse adjoint with the sub-preconditioner set to LU together with the liaison's transonic preconditioner lead, neither of which has ever been set on our M6 runs, to learn whether the conditioning block that predates the sub-LU tool still stands
rationale: A3 closed as blocked: adjoint breakdown at every mesh size tested, regardless of memory headroom. But the block predates the sub-LU unblock that later cleared the incompressible family, and that unblock was never carried to M6; separately, the liaison's research found the official transonic tutorial setting a transonic preconditioner option our M6 records never set. That is a gap, not a verdict, and one arm on the cheapest mesh closes it either way: convergence reopens the A3 ladder and gives the breakdown story its epilogue, and a second breakdown confirms the conditioning wall beyond the incompressible family with both known unblocks tested
gate: One adjoint solve on the vcoarse M6 mesh with the sub-preconditioner set to LU and the transonic preconditioner option set as the official transonic tutorial sets it, nothing else changed from the archived arm. Outcome one: the adjoint converges, the A3 ladder reopens, and the breakdown record gains an epilogue naming the settings that were missing. Outcome two: the adjoint breaks down again, and the conditioning wall is confirmed beyond the incompressible family, with both known unblocks on the record as tested and insufficient
cost_basis: estimate, the review's figure: the vcoarse M6 adjoint has run before and failed by breakdown rather than by walltime, and the two settings change conditioning rather than problem size, so the archived arm's spend is the anchor
expected_knowledge_gain: Either the A3 ladder reopened by a setting that already existed, which converts a blocked family into a running one for the cost of a single arm, or the conditioning wall confirmed as real beyond the incompressible family, which is the epilogue the breakdown record currently lacks

decision_note: supervisor review 2026-08-07 under Katie's standing green light
outcome: NOT EVALUABLE AT THE VCOARSE RUNG, pre-registered branch, neither gate outcome claimed. The arm never reached the adjoint or the primal: DAFoam's mesh-quality gate rejected the archived vcoarse mesh (23 negative-volume cells, max aspect ratio 2.08e+95, max non-orthogonality 135.3 deg, 144 wrong face pyramids, Failed 5 mesh checks), and the defect is proven congenital -- the preserved July-28 pre-repair decomposition carries the identical 23 negatives to the last digit, all clumped at the pyHyp tip trailing-edge collapse on the 4x-coarsened surface (generator-owned). The record's old SEGV/corrupted-field story is rediagnosed en route: two orphan autoPatches (auto4/auto5, the wing lower surface and TE base) that the tutorial createPatchDict never mapped; the pre-registered patch merge repaired that cleanly and the run got past the old failure point. Both levers therefore remain untested on M6 and the question stays open; bonus finding recorded in the pre-registration: every archived M6/A6 script's transonicPCOption: 2 is dead code for DARhoSimpleCFoam (only ==1 exists in DAResidualRhoSimpleCFoam.C:173), so no archived M6 run ever had an active transonic PC. Re-file candidates reported, not run: the 21,840-cell sweep mesh (passes the gate, carries the -5 on record) or a regenerated vcoarse from a 3x surface. Spend: 0.53 of 30 core-min on the arm proper. Pre-reg 12d3a7a3 (02:29:17Z, before launch t0 02:30:51Z); result A3_SUBLU_RESULT.md, 54a2f2ff. || RE-FILE OUTCOME (chief-approved same session, 21,840-cell sweep mesh, prereg 054d10b2 + addenda f77b2607/7f207f65): NOT EVALUABLE ON THIS HOST, neither gate outcome claimed -- both levers were proven ACTIVE in-log for the first time on any M6 run (transonicPCOption 1 echoed in the DAOption dump; the sub-LU banner at PC setup), and the sub-LU complete-LU factorization then proved memory-infeasible at this rung: oom-killed at a 10g cap, and at 20g it grazed the cap, drove the 30 GB host to 12 GB swap and a 2 GB MemAvailable floor breach, completing zero 100-iteration KSP blocks in 27.9 min before the host-protection kill (family precedent). Interpretation stated rather than hidden: a memory death cannot confirm a CONDITIONING wall -- the two blockers are separate per the envelope record -- so the -5 question stays open. Spend 127.5 of 30 core-min, overrun inside the pre-registered runs-to-reason-codes commitment, terminated only by the host floor. Named follow-ups, not run: transonicPCOption:1 alone (fits in the record's 5.9 GiB, ~28 core-min) or sub-LU at np=8/16 to shrink the ASM blocks. Result appended to A3_SUBLU_RESULT.md, 0b4f3005. || TPC1-ALONE OUTCOME (chief ruling 1, prereg 13c244cd, launch t0 03:24:06Z): CONVERGED -- PetscConvergedReason 2 on BOTH solves (CD 368 iterations to 2.045e-06, CL 383 iterations 1.839e-01 to 1.831e-05), rc=0, 110 s = 7.33 of ~28 core-min, stock ILU (zero sub-LU banner, env unset), cold-started, healthy norms with no denormal false-success. ENTRY 8 OUTCOME ONE FIRES: the A3 ladder reopens and the DIVERGED_BREAKDOWN story has its epilogue -- the record's wall at this rung was the INACTIVE transonic PC (every archived M6 -5 carried transonicPCOption: 2 as dead code); one token, 2 -> 1, converts the double -5 into double reason-2 on the identical configuration, and the record CL solve's 300-iteration stall value 1.839160961071e-01 is this arm's own starting residual to four digits before it descends through. First M6-family adjoint convergence and first M6 gradient in the lab's history. Scope: one rung (21,840 cells); taller rungs and the family FD-verification rule are the reopened ladder's next tasks; sub-LU np=8/16 stays DEFERRED per ruling 2, now a curiosity not a blocker. Result in A3_SUBLU_RESULT.md, 11b90d25. || EPILOGUE RULINGS EXECUTED (14d57c8e): (1) NEGATIVE CONTROL (prereg 31eede16) -- the record transonicPCOption:2 config reruns on today's host and reproduces the double -5 BIT-FOR-BIT (solve 1 iteration-0 residual and solve 2's entire stall sequence match the 2026-07-30 record to every printed digit, cold signature bit-identical to the converged arm); causation nailed on the single token; 8.53 core-min; result 551a7ba5. (2) FD VERIFICATION (prereg 4aef4a2f + addendum b9f42631) -- ARM PASS per the pre-registered bands: AoA 0.18 percent and the true max-gradient shape component 0.93 percent vs central FD sized off the measured noise floor; two small-signal components step-inconsistent and unverdicted; adjoint bit-reproducible across three runs at 368 iterations; the prereg's shape[5] reference number corrected as a disclosed wrapped-numpy mis-parse (true max-|g| is shape[115]); the M6 gradient is no longer an existence proof; 29.5 core-min; result e4280b79. (3) WARM-START AUDIT executed and closed done (WARMSTART_AUDIT.md 9bb948b2, guidelines section 8 ccf18d2f, proposal d7d38f5a): all record-grade conclusions cold-clean, two non-overturning warm flags. || RUNG 2 (42,120 cells, prereg 22c8e988 + addendum 2b3e6517, result 4e982b4a): CONVERGED + FD PASS -- both adjoint solves reason 2 (CD 987 iterations, CL 1171 to 1.8246e-05) and all three FD components evaluable, step-consistent and passing (patchV[1] 0.0077%, twist[1] 0.2740%, shape[115] 0.0172% vs a 8.09e-07 noise floor). THE LADDER HAS TWO VERIFIED RUNGS and the mesh-size question opens honestly. Attempt 1's CL -3 at the default 1000-iteration cap was refused as a wall reading and proven a pure budget knob: attempt 2 reproduces its iteration-1000 residual to TEN significant digits (1.307615740828e-04 vs 1.307615741156e-04) then converges. The mesh was quarantined under MESH_STANDARD v1.1 (no certificate) and was certified first -- verdict clean, certificate_admits True, independently replicated digit-for-digit by a second agent's own checkMesh. Measured pricing basis for rung 3: iterations scale at cells^1.50 (CD) / cells^1.70 (CL), so 79,560 cells needs gmresMaxIters >= 4000 and ~113 core-min -- pricing off cells alone underestimates, which is why rung 2 ran 99.5 core-min against a 47 estimate. Rung 3 not launched; it is the chief's call. || RUNG 3 (79,560 cells, prereg 3e585b07, result 834574a6): DIVERGED BY STAGNATION -- the reopened ladder has a CEILING, bracketed between 42,120 and 79,560 cells. Stage 0 (mandatory transfer test) FAILED: Richardson collapsed at rung 2 to exactly 0.0 at iteration 200, the first restart boundary, so the lever was withdrawn and rung 3 ran baseline. Stage 1: CD hit the 4000 cap at reason -3 with the residual FLAT to six significant figures over 2,700 iterations (3.79e-07 relative change; corrected same day from an initial "nine", which was false precision -- the reduction figures and verdict are unaffected) (1.31x total reduction vs rung 2's 1407x), CL never attempted; the budget-vs-wall distinction pre-registered before either was seen resolves rung 2's -3 as budget and this one as the wall. NOT a memory death (11.65 of 22 GiB, host never below 17 GB), which is what makes the conditioning verdict sayable. The iteration exponent (cells^1.50/1.70) BREAKS at the next doubling by kind, not degree: a two-point slope in this family is a description of two points, not a cost law, and extrapolation to the 399,360-cell class is foreclosed by measurement. Stage 2 FD arm correctly not launched (conditional on stage 1 converging), so 111.0 of the approved 170-190 core-min were spent. Bonus, same session: the chief's FD-1/FD-2 provenance rider ridden inside the running container -- FD-1 CONFIRMED with reproducible provenance, FD-2 REFUTED in both images (SIMPLEC IS implemented at pEqnSimple.H:27 and DAResidualSimpleFoam.C:189; the original verdict came from an include-blind grep), retracting A4's stated cause for its 22.05% gap (7ca80f8d, 35a91e0e). || RESTART CHALLENGE (adversarial defense of my own ceiling claim, prereg 85a56e40, result 0dc6a050): BRANCH B -- THE CEILING HARDENS. gmresRestart 200->1000 (5x window, +4.6 GB of Krylov vectors, affordable where Richardson was not) moved the CD residual at the pre-fixed iteration-1000 checkpoint from 1.615247229756e-02 to 9.804385762596e-03 -- 1.647x against a pre-registered 10x materiality bar, below even the 2x-5x nudge the pre-registration had ruled branch B in advance. Disclosed against my own claim: the restart effect is REAL (descent persisted through the uninterrupted 1000-iteration cycle where the 200-window went flat by ~500, then flattened at exactly iteration 1000, the restart boundary) -- but a 5x window buying 1.6x, with ~20,000+ further iterations needed at the observed rate, is a ceiling and not a budget. Stated uncertainty: this excludes a restart-budget artifact at an affordable window, not a restart-free method. Memory prediction 16.3 GiB vs 15.76 GiB measured (3.3% error). 47.7 core-min, inside the 66-82 estimate. The rung-3 ceiling claim (834574a6) stands unmodified, now having survived the one challenge whose mechanism matched its failure mode. || A3 LINE CLOSED 2026-08-10. Saad proof arm: PROOF CLAUSE NOT MET (prereg a9bb202d, outcome 368996c3) -- the diagonal-spread route named in the capability strategy is a measured DEAD END (rung 2 spreads 14.40 decades and converges, rung 3 spreads 14.47 and cannot), and the chosen asmOverlap remedy's own falsifier fired (kappa 0.979x/1.062x, residual 3% worse). Fill-1 ENGINEERING arm (prereg d4c706e8, result 48b34cbf, explicitly outside the proof): STALLS at 1.859x against a pre-registered 10x bar, becoming the ninth refuted candidate, so the ceiling stands UNQUALIFIED. Surprise recorded honestly: ILU(1) improves the mid-cycle preconditioned condition estimate by ~10^7 (4.69e10 -> 1.66e3) and still buys only 1.9x, so the Krylov condition estimate is not predicting convergence here; a non-normality reading would explain the whole elimination table and is explicitly NOT claimed, being untested. Capability-boundary defect candidate prepared FILING-READY, NOT FILED (f29378d9): DAFoam calls KSPSetFromOptions then overrides ksp_type/pc_type/sub_pc_type at twelve call sites, so a user who diagnoses their conditioning correctly cannot act on it -- monitors work while remedies are silently discarded. Spend across both arms 95.5 core-min, flagged progressively before each launch. || CAPSTONE: NON-NORMALITY DIAGNOSTIC (prereg 7783f603, result 15b64e81, 0 of a 25 core-min cap -- both operators were already on disk). Reading (i) refuted first at zero cost: within-run variability of the Krylov condition estimate is at most 6.5x (2.22x/6.51x/2.32x across three arms) against a fill0-to-fill1 jump of ~2.5e7, six to seven orders apart, so the estimate being a subspace lower bound cannot explain it. Reading (ii) then REFUTED by measurement: normalized Frobenius departure from normality (Hutchinson, k=200, four spmv per probe) gives nu_F = 2.651122e-03 at the STALLING rung against 4.298842e-03 at the CONVERGING one -- ratio 0.617 against a pre-registered 3.0 bar, confidence intervals non-overlapping, so the stalling rung is measurably LESS non-normal, not more. The hypothesis my own fill-1 arm generated is refuted by my own follow-up. Non-normality becomes the TENTH eliminated candidate. Limitation stated: this measures the assembled preconditioner dRdWTPC, not the matrix-free Jacobian nor A*M^-1, which this build never assembles. The mechanism remains unknown and is now precisely bounded rather than vaguely open. || ESCAPE HATCH RESTORED AND THE UNREACHABLE CLASS TESTED (prereg bfe9a1ef/a15b839d, results 0fcc98a0/e1755100). Stage 1: DALinearEqn.C patched so KSPSetFromOptions is called last (28-line diff, image dafoam-kspopts:v1, both prior images intact), three AD targets rebuilt in 29 s. GATE A REGRESSION PASSED BIT-IDENTICALLY -- rung 1 returns CD 368 / CL 383 reason 2 with the cold signature to 16 digits, so honouring the option channel is measured NOT load-bearing and the upstream fix survives a maintainer's first objection. GATE B PASSED: ksp_view reports fgmres where the shipped build reports gmres. Two upstream findings: overriding ksp_type resets DAFoam's restart to PETSc's default 30 (cost a 368-iteration convergence in the test), and printInfo still echoes daOptions rather than effective values -- the L-40 hazard found inside the upstream code, so the recommendation became fix (a) PLUS an effective-value echo. Stage 2, the first test of the previously-unreachable class: lgmres (restart carried explicitly per the Gate B lesson, verified restart=200 in ksp_view) finished 5.10x WORSE than the control and 3.88x above its own start; gamg (verified 4-level hierarchy) DIVERGED to 7.55e+179 at reason -5 with memory never a factor at 7.0 GiB. ELEVENTH AND TWELFTH ELIMINATIONS. Bounded per the binding: the shipped-toolchain ceiling verdict is untouched, and this tested two OFF-THE-SHELF members at documented defaults, not the class tuned for a convection-dominated nonsymmetric adjoint. Third instance of the standing caveat: the Krylov condition estimate spanned six orders across arms (2.70e5, 9.57e10, 7.71e17) whose behaviour ranged only from stalling to worse. Spend: stage 1 21.5 of 15, stage 2 124.4 of 52, the overrun being gamg alone at 4.1x because both arms were priced off the ILU per-iteration basis and AMG setup has no relation to it. The A3 line rests here.
